game: IND at PIT, Week 9 2025, kickoff 2025-11-02 13:00 ET, outdoor Pittsburgh, PIT +3.5, total 51.5, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Books have Indianapolis laying 3.5 with implied totals IND 27.5 and PIT 24.0 in a 51.5 outdoor game, so a competitive high-play script, not a blowout. IND leads by about a score late and closes with Jonathan Taylor, who has 49 carries for 370 rush yards plus 9 targets for 73 receiving yards over weeks 6-8. Pittsburgh, a 3.5-point dog, throws more, and DK Metcalf (21 targets, 200 yards, 313 air yards in that window) is the shot-play. Both implied totals in the mid-20s keep pace up and starter snaps alive.
script.flip1: IND gets up big early and grinds the clock: Taylor's carries spike, Daniel Jones and the Colts receivers stall the way a favorite's passing stats die in a clock-kill, and PIT abandons the run so Jaylen Warren's recent 13-carry pace (40 carries, 241 yards over weeks 6-8) dies while Metcalf, Freiermuth (11 targets, 135 yards) and Jonnu Smith (13 targets, 63 yards) see more targets.
script.flip2: Shootout or Pittsburgh leads: both teams throw, Taylor's rush line falls toward the 66-yard game in his last four, and Alec Pierce (476 air yards on 19 targets over weeks 6-8) and Metcalf only clear if pressure does not get home. An unsaved outdoor slog would also drag the 51.5 total down and miss both yardage overs.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report, inactives not yet locked (90-minute list not in the pack). IND out: DE Samson Ebukam (knee), DE Tyquan Lewis (groin), WR Anthony Gould (knee). IND questionable: DT Grover Stewart (foot). Gould is not in the weeks 6-8 target leaders (Pittman 21, Pierce 19, Tyler Warren 19, Downs 10), so his absence does not create a new WR1. The two edge rushers out, plus Stewart questionable, thin the Colts front: Pittsburgh should see less pressure and a softer run fit, which helps Aaron Rodgers' time to throw, DK Metcalf's deep shots, and Jaylen Warren's rushing efficiency. PIT out: S Jabrill Peppers (quad), CB Cory Trice Jr. (hamstring), WR Scott Miller (finger). PIT questionable: S Chuck Clark (illness), LB Cole Holcomb (illness), LB Malik Harrison (knee), QB Will Howard (hand). Howard is the backup; Rodgers is the weeks 6-8 quarterback (2 carries, 7 yards) and is not listed out. Peppers out and Clark questionable thin the safeties, and Trice out thins the corner group, which helps IND deep and outside shots (Pierce 476 air yards, Pittman 21 targets) if Jones has time. Holcomb and Harrison both questionable is the linebacker fallout: backups would help Tyler Warren and Taylor as checkdowns and could loosen run fits. Miller out is a depth WR, same as Gould; Roman Wilson (8 targets, 103 yards) and Calvin Austin are the next names, not a role change we can price. matchup.pressure: PIT blitz rate 39 percent. IND EPA per dropback is 0.17 versus the blitz and 0.35 with no blitz, so pressure hurts Jones and should cut deep yards while boosting RB and TE checkdowns. IND blitz rate is only 27 percent, and PIT EPA per dropback is 0.13 versus the blitz and 0.10 with none, so Rodgers is not blitz-sensitive. Ebukam and Lewis both out should push actual pressure on Rodgers even lower than that 27 percent.
matchup.bleeds: PIT bleeds the middle (9.09 YPA) and has allowed 22 runs of 10-plus and 25 passes of 20-plus for 295 yards in 7 games, with rush YPC allowed 4.47. IND has allowed 20 runs of 10-plus and 28 passes of 20-plus for 334 yards in 8 games, rush YPC allowed 4.32, stingiest YPA on the right at 6.21.
matchup.overlap: The cleanest IND overlap is Tyler Warren (19 targets, 185 yards, 112 air yards over weeks 6-8) into that PIT middle, with Taylor as the blitz checkdown (9 targets) and Pierce as the deep beneficiary of Peppers and Trice being out if Jones has time, which the 39 percent blitz fights. The overlap that also fits the dog-throw script is Metcalf (21 targets, 313 air yards) into an IND defense that has allowed 28 explosives, with extra time because both Colts edges are out. Warren's schematic overlap was not taken as a leg because his last four receiving lines are 44, 63, 69 and 53 against 66.5.

data_check.notes: Step 8 is incomplete on purpose: no sims, no projection file, and no Pinnacle or other two-sided prices, so model_p values are discounted hand estimates from the last-four role, not 3-sim probabilities, and neither leg can beat a no-vig by 3 points because no-vig is N/A. Stand-in lines are 2025 season-to-date medians, not shopped market numbers. Recent form agrees with both sides (Taylor weeks 6-8 rush-plus-rec about 148 versus 125.5, three of last four over; Metcalf weeks 6-8 about 66.7 versus 55.5). The disagreeing piece, which is why this is a flag and not a cut, is efficiency: PIT has allowed 4.47 YPC, so a full cool-down from Taylor's 7.55 YPC over 49 carries can land under 125.5, and 125.5 is his own median stand-in. That flags the strong read for the human; it does not delete it. pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. Taylor: Pittsburgh sold out to stop him, the 7.55 yards per carry from weeks 6-8 regressed toward the 4.47 PIT has allowed, he finished nearer the 66-rush and 86 rush-plus-rec game, and Jones' checkdowns went to Tyler Warren (19 targets) or Downs (10 targets) instead of Taylor's 9. Metcalf: the 126 and 95 were one-play spikes on 313 air yards, an IND secondary with no corner listed out held him to the 50 and 55 already in his last four, and Pittsburgh stayed close enough with Jaylen Warren (40 carries, 241 yards) and a shorthanded Colts front that Rodgers never had to air it out. Shared kill: an unsaved November outdoor forecast turned 51.5 into a low-30s game and neither yardage prop had the plays. The counter-case is real on efficiency, which is why Taylor is flagged rather than sized, but it is not stronger than the role-plus-script read, so the leg stays for the human.
slip_story: One story only: competitive IND -3.5 in a 51.5 game, Colts lead late without a blowout. Taylor rush-plus-rec over is the favorite-touches leg (late carries plus checkdowns into a 39 percent blitz). Metcalf receiving over is the dog-throws correlate. They cash together in the base script and in a shootout. Do not add Colts WR overs, which need the pass-heavy flip, and do not add a total under. Two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player, no depth receivers. Candidates only. The price gate was not run, no stake, no bet.
